title: DC vs AC Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's torch runs on a cell, but his table fan runs from the wall socket. Both use electric current, so why can't the fan just run on a cell? In this animated lesson we compare direct current (DC), which flows in one direction only, with alternating current (AC), which keeps reversing as a smooth sine wave made by a coil turning in a magnetic field.

On a live breadboard the same resistor and indicator lamp run first from a cell (steady electrons, a flat line on the oscilloscope) and then from an AC source in slow motion (electrons rocking back and forth, a sine wave on the scope, the reading swinging from plus to minus). We define the cycle, the period T and the frequency f = 1/T, show why every cycle has two reversals, and work out the period and reversals of India's 230 V, 50 Hz mains. Then why homes get AC (transformers and high-voltage lines) while phones need DC, the exam trap (50 Hz means 100 reversals a second), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 7 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 2: Principles of Electricity, Network Theorems and AC Principles (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
